name: Aqara Radiator Thermostat E1 (EU)

matter.note: Aqara says Matter support would come later as an OTA update of a compatible Aqara hub. No CSA listing was found for the E1 itself.

apple_home.note: Aqara lists HomeKit support, exposed through an Aqara hub.

google_home.note: Aqara lists Google support through the Aqara hub.

alexa.note: Aqara lists Alexa support through the Aqara hub.

smartthings.note: Not on Aqara's platform list as seen in search results.

home_assistant.note: Aqara's launch release lists Home Assistant and says support comes through the HomeKit Controller integration, which pairs with the Aqara hub's HomeKit bridge. Direct Zigbee pairing is not documented by Aqara.

hubRequired.note: Aqara says an Aqara Zigbee 3.0 hub is required and sold separately.

localControl.note: No Aqara page seen describes hub-local control.

systems.value: M30 × 1.5 valves; RA, RAV, RAVL adapters included
systems.note: Retailers say manual, return-temperature-limiter and monotube systems are not supported; not confirmed on an Aqara page.

power.note: Aqara's spec page lists two 1.5 V AA batteries (included) and claims up to a year of battery life, depending on use.

summary: Zigbee, not Thread: the Aqara Radiator Thermostat E1 only reaches Apple Home, Google Home and Alexa through an Aqara Zigbee 3.0 hub, which is sold separately. Home Assistant works via the HomeKit Controller integration on that hub's HomeKit bridge. The valve fits M30 × 1.5 with RA, RAV and RAVL adapters included, and takes 2 × AA batteries (included) for up to a year. Aqara says Matter may arrive later through a hub update.
caveats: Needs an Aqara Zigbee 3.0 hub, sold separately.
Matter was announced as a future hub update; it is not confirmed on Aqara pages seen.

sources.title: Aqara Adds a Smart Radiator Thermostat to its Product Portfolio
